earnings.title: VIPER ENERGY, INC., A SUBSIDIARY OF DIAMONDBACK ENERGY, INC., REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL AND OPERATING RESULTS
highlights: Net income of $300 million; Net income margin of 45%
Cash flows from operating activities of $447 million; Operating cash flow margin of 68%
Free Cash Flow 1 of $520 million; Free Cash Flow margin 1 of 79%
Declared Q3 2026 base cash dividend of $0.50 per Class A common share
Repurchased approximately 2.1 million Class A shares for approximately $90 million

quotes.text: Viper’s momentum carried through the third quarter, with average daily oil production growing more than six percent quarter over quarter on the strength of recent acquisitions and continued development activity from both Diamondback and our third-party operators.
quotes.by: Kaes Van’t Hof, Chief Executive Officer of Viper

outlook: Approximately 20% of Midland Basin acreage in units with zero producing horizontal wells; expected to support efficient full stack development in coming years
Expect pro forma net debt at year end 2026 of approximately $2.4 billion, equating to pro forma leverage of approximately 1.0x last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA

items.heading: Geopolitics and market conditions for oil and natural gas, and particularly volatility in prices for oil and natural gas, have in the past adversely affected, and may in the future adversely affect, our revenue, cash flows, profitability, growth and production.

Our commodity price derivatives could result in financial losses, may fail to protect us from declines in commodity prices, prevent us from fully benefiting from commodity price increases and may expose us to other risks, including counterparty credit risk.
The risks relating to the transition to a low carbon economy could impose new costs on our operations that may have a material and adverse effect on us.
Changing political and social perspectives on climate change and other environmental, social and governance factors may create risks and uncertainties impacting our business.
Increased costs of capital could adversely affect our business.

We may not have sufficient available cash to pay any quarterly dividend on our Common Stock, our cash available for dividends may vary significantly from quarter to quarter and our board of directors may in the future modify or revoke our cash dividend policy at any time at its discretion. Our dividend policy could limit our ability to grow and make acquisitions.
